description: Student developer passionate about AI, machine learning, and software engineering. I'm building GHOST IN THE DATA, an intelligent Mars exploration project for NASA Space Apps. Looking for motivated teammates interested in AI/ML, Python, computer vision, 3D development, geospatial mapping, astronomy, or UI/UX. Curiosity, creativity, and teamwork matter most!
summary:
GHOST is an AI-assisted Martian exploration platform that helps users discover, analyze, and investigate scientifically interesting locations on Mars. It combines real Martian imagery, machine-learning techniques, route planning, and interactive 3D visualization in one exploration workflow.

Through three connected stages—Discover, Understand, and Investigate—users can identify potential targets, examine available evidence, and plan routes across the Martian surface. GHOST demonstrates how AI and planetary science data can make Mars exploration more systematic, accessible, and informed.
details:
GHOST is an AI-assisted Martian exploration platform that helps users discover, analyze, and investigate scientifically interesting locations on Mars.

The platform follows three connected stages: Discover, Understand, and Investigate. It identifies potentially interesting surface targets using image analysis and anomaly detection, allows users to examine available imagery and scientific information, and helps plan exploration routes using the A* path-planning algorithm.

GHOST combines DINOv2-Small for image feature extraction, Isolation Forest for anomaly detection, and a 5-Nearest Neighbors approach with depth features for synthetic rover perception. Its interactive 3D environment allows users to explore Martian locations and connect scientific evidence with route planning.

The project was developed using Python, FastAPI, React, Next.js, TypeScript, CesiumJS, PyTorch, and scikit-learn.

During validation, GHOST processed 409 real Martian targets and successfully planned a 25.93 km exploration route. Its anomaly-detection evaluation achieved an AUROC of 0.937 on 55 samples containing planted anomalies. The rover-perception component is synthetic and has not yet been validated using real rover imagery or physical rover tests.

Our goal is to make planetary exploration more systematic and accessible by bringing together AI, planetary data, and interactive geospatial technology.
